title: Appeals Court Reduces Le Pen's Ineligibility Sentence, Clearing Her for 2027 Race
detail: The Paris Court of Appeal upheld Marine Le Pen's conviction for embezzling European Parliament funds in the Rassemblement National assistants affair but significantly reduced her sentence: three years in prison (two suspended, one under electronic monitoring) and 45 months of ineligibility, 30 of them suspended. The firm portion of the ineligibility penalty — reduced to 15 months — was deemed already served, having run out on June 30 under the provisional-execution order from the first-instance verdict. The ruling clears Le Pen to run in the April–May 2027 presidential election; she immediately confirmed her candidacy and announced she would still appeal to the Court of Cassation. The first-instance court had barred her from running for five years with immediate effect.

media.caption: French court upholds Le Pen's fraud conviction but reduces ineligibility, clearing her 2027 bid

title: Macron Nominates Senator Buffet as Défenseur des Droits, Sparking Backlash
detail: President Macron proposed Les Républicains senator François-Noël Buffet, prefect-turned-lawmaker from the Rhône, to succeed Claire Hédon as Défenseur des Droits (national ombudsman) when her six-year mandate expires in late July. The nomination drew immediate opposition from more than 50 associations — including Greenpeace France, SOS Racisme, and Planning Familial — and over 110,000 petition signatures within days, citing Buffet's past votes against marriage equality and medically assisted reproduction, and his support for tougher migration policy. Left-wing parties called the choice a "provocation." The Senate and National Assembly law committees were scheduled to hear Buffet and vote on the nomination on July 15, with a two-thirds majority needed to reject it.

media.caption: François-Noël Buffet proposed by Emmanuel Macron to become Défenseur des Droits
